_help: Track A: Nominalisation. Items are grouped by stage. See README.md, section 'How to add or edit an item'.
title: Nominalisation

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “analyse” (verb)?
items.reason: Verbs ending in -yse often become nouns ending in -ysis: analyse → analysis.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “significant” (adjective)?
items.reason: Adjectives ending in -ant usually become nouns ending in -ance.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “develop” (verb)?
items.reason: Many verbs add -ment to become a noun: develop → development.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “reduce” (verb)?
items.reason: Verbs ending in -duce become nouns ending in -duction: reduce → reduction.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “decide” (verb)?
items.reason: Verbs ending in -ide often become nouns ending in -ision: decide → decision.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “grow” (verb)?
items.reason: Some short verbs add -th: grow → growth (like strong → strength).

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “accurate” (adjective)?
items.reason: Adjectives ending in -ate often become nouns ending in -acy: accurate → accuracy.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “available” (adjective)?
items.reason: Adjectives ending in -able become nouns ending in -ability.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “fail” (verb)?
items.reason: The noun from “fail” is “failure” (-ure ending), not “failing”.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “behave” (verb)?
items.reason: behave → behaviour. Australian spelling keeps the u: behaviour.

items.prompt: What is the noun form of “efficient” (adjective)?
items.reason: Adjectives ending in -ent often become nouns ending in -ency.

items.prompt: What is the verb form of “investment” (noun)?
items.reason: Take away the -ment ending to get the verb: investment → invest.

items.prompt: What is the adjective form of “complexity” (noun)?
items.reason: Take away the -ity ending to get the adjective: complexity → complex.

items.prompt: What is the verb form of “emphasis” (noun)?
items.reason: emphasis → emphasise. Australian spelling uses -ise.

items.prompt: The rapid expansion of online study has increased the flexibility of university courses.
items.reason: “expansion” comes from the verb expand; “flexibility” comes from the adjective flexible.
items.hint: There are two. Look for -sion and -ity.

items.prompt: The council's decision to raise fees caused strong disagreement among local shop owners.
items.reason: “decision” comes from decide; “disagreement” comes from disagree.
items.hint: There are two. Look for -sion and -ment.

items.prompt: Poor ventilation in classrooms can reduce the concentration of students.
items.reason: “ventilation” comes from ventilate; “concentration” comes from concentrate.
items.hint: There are two. Both end in -tion.

items.prompt: The introduction of electric buses has led to a noticeable improvement in the air around schools.
items.reason: “introduction” comes from introduce; “improvement” comes from improve.
items.hint: There are two. Look for -tion and -ment.

items.prompt: Regular exercise contributes to the prevention of heart disease and the reduction of stress.
items.reason: “prevention” comes from prevent; “reduction” comes from reduce.
items.hint: There are two. Both end in -tion.

items.prompt:
Which sentence sounds more academic, and why?
A: Because people used more cars, the air got worse.
B: Increased car use led to a decline in air quality.
options: B, because it turns the actions into noun phrases (“increased car use”, “a decline”).
A, because it explains the cause with “because”.
B, because it has more words.
acceptedAnswers: B, because it turns the actions into noun phrases (“increased car use”, “a decline”).
items.reason: B packs “people used more cars” and “got worse” into noun phrases, which is typical of academic writing.
items.hint: Look for the sentence with fewer verbs and more noun phrases.

items.prompt:
Which sentence sounds more academic, and why?
A: The company grew quickly, and this surprised investors.
B: The rapid growth of the company surprised investors.
options: B, because “grew quickly” becomes the noun phrase “rapid growth”.
A, because it joins two clauses with “and”.
B, because it uses the word “investors”.
acceptedAnswers: B, because “grew quickly” becomes the noun phrase “rapid growth”.
items.reason: B turns the verb “grew” into the noun “growth”, so two clauses become one.
items.hint: Which sentence has one clause instead of two?

items.prompt:
Which sentence sounds more academic, and why?
A: The failure of the policy was due to a lack of funding.
B: The policy failed because there was not enough money.
options: A, because it packs the actions into nouns (“failure”, “lack of funding”).
B, because “because” is more formal than “due to”.
A, because it is longer.
acceptedAnswers: A, because it packs the actions into nouns (“failure”, “lack of funding”).
items.reason: A uses the nouns “failure” and “lack” instead of the verb “failed” and the phrase “there was not enough”.
items.hint: Which sentence uses -ure and other noun forms?

items.prompt:
Which sentence sounds more academic, and why?
A: When students are anxious, they often perform badly in exams.
B: Student anxiety often leads to poor exam performance.
options: B, because the adjective “anxious” and the verb “perform” become nouns (“anxiety”, “performance”).
A, because it starts with “When”.
A, because it uses the word “often”.
acceptedAnswers: B, because the adjective “anxious” and the verb “perform” become nouns (“anxiety”, “performance”).
items.reason: B turns “are anxious” into “anxiety” and “perform” into “performance”.

items.prompt:
Which sentence sounds more academic, and why?
A: The introduction of the new timetable caused confusion among staff.
B: The school introduced a new timetable, and the staff were confused.
options: A, because “introduced” and “were confused” become nouns (“introduction”, “confusion”).
B, because it names the school.
B, because it has two verbs.
acceptedAnswers: A, because “introduced” and “were confused” become nouns (“introduction”, “confusion”).
items.reason: A uses the nouns “introduction” and “confusion”, so the idea fits into one clause.

items.prompt: Energy prices went up sharply, so many families struggled.
items.frame: The sharp ___ in energy ___ caused hardship for many families.
modelAnswers: The sharp increase in energy prices caused hardship for many families.
items.reason: “went up” becomes the noun “increase” (or “rise”), so the sentence needs only one main verb: caused.
items.hint: The first gap is a noun for “go up”.

items.prompt: The city's population grew quickly, and housing became harder to find.
items.frame: The rapid ___ of the city's population reduced the ___ of housing.
modelAnswers: The rapid growth of the city's population reduced the availability of housing.
items.reason: “grew” becomes “growth”, and “harder to find” becomes “reduced the availability”.
items.hint: The second gap comes from the adjective “available”.

items.prompt: When teachers respond quickly, students improve faster.
items.frame: A quick ___ from teachers leads to faster ___ in students' work.
modelAnswers: A quick response from teachers leads to faster improvement in students' work.
items.reason: “respond” becomes “response” and “improve” becomes “improvement”.

items.prompt: The factory closed, and many people lost their jobs.
items.frame: The ___ of the factory resulted in the ___ of many jobs.
modelAnswers: The closure of the factory resulted in the loss of many jobs.
items.reason: “closed” becomes “closure” and “lost” becomes “loss”.

items.prompt: Scientists analysed the data carefully, and they found a clear pattern.
items.frame: Careful ___ of the data led to the ___ of a clear pattern.
modelAnswers: Careful analysis of the data led to the discovery of a clear pattern.
items.reason: “analysed” becomes “analysis” and “found” becomes “discovery”.

items.prompt: Employees are more satisfied when managers communicate clearly.
modelAnswers: Clear communication from managers increases employee satisfaction.
items.reason: “communicate” becomes “communication” and “satisfied” becomes “satisfaction”.

items.prompt: People are increasingly worried that the internet is not secure.
items.frame: There is growing ___ about the lack of internet ___.
modelAnswers: There is growing concern about the lack of internet security.
items.reason: “worried” becomes “concern” and “secure” becomes “security”.
items.hint: The second gap comes from the adjective “secure”.

items.prompt: Students who attend lectures regularly usually achieve higher marks.
items.frame: Regular ___ at lectures is usually linked to higher ___.
modelAnswers: Regular attendance at lectures is usually linked to higher achievement.
items.reason: “attend” becomes “attendance” and “achieve” becomes “achievement”.

items.prompt: The government invested more in public transport, which reduced traffic.
items.frame: Greater ___ in public transport led to a ___ in traffic.
modelAnswers: Greater investment in public transport led to a reduction in traffic.
items.reason: “invested” becomes “investment” and “reduced” becomes “reduction”.

items.prompt: People use more cars, so the air gets worse.
modelAnswers: Increased car use leads to a decline in air quality.
Greater car use results in poorer air quality.
items.reason: The two clauses become noun phrases (“increased car use”, “a decline in air quality”) joined by one verb.
items.hint: Turn “use more cars” into a noun phrase, then link it with “leads to”.

items.prompt: Many students leave university because they cannot pay the fees.
modelAnswers: The inability to pay fees causes many students to leave university.
Financial difficulty leads many students to withdraw from university.
items.reason: “cannot pay” becomes the noun phrase “the inability to pay” or “financial difficulty”.
items.hint: Start with a noun phrase for “cannot pay”.

items.prompt: When companies advertise online, they sell more products.
modelAnswers: Online advertising leads to higher sales.
Online advertising increases product sales.
items.reason: “advertise” becomes “advertising” and “sell more” becomes “higher sales”.

items.prompt: Children who sleep well can concentrate better at school.
modelAnswers: Good sleep improves children's concentration at school.
Adequate sleep leads to better concentration in children at school.
items.reason: “sleep well” becomes “good sleep” and “concentrate” becomes “concentration”.

items.prompt: The climate is changing, and this is affecting how farmers grow food.
modelAnswers: Climate change is affecting food production.
Climate change is having an effect on agricultural production.
items.reason: “The climate is changing” becomes “climate change”, and “how farmers grow food” becomes “food production”.

items.prompt: If hospitals have more nurses, patients recover faster.
modelAnswers: Higher nurse staffing levels lead to faster patient recovery.
An increase in nursing staff results in quicker patient recovery.
items.reason: “recover faster” becomes “faster patient recovery”, linked by “lead to”.

items.prompt: Workers are happier when they can choose their own hours.
modelAnswers: Flexible working hours increase employee satisfaction.
The freedom to choose working hours improves worker satisfaction.
items.reason: “are happier” becomes “satisfaction” and “can choose” becomes “flexible hours” or “the freedom to choose”.

items.prompt: Cities are growing quickly, and this puts pressure on water supplies.
modelAnswers: Rapid urban growth puts pressure on water supplies.
The rapid growth of cities increases pressure on water supplies.
items.reason: “Cities are growing quickly” becomes “rapid urban growth”.

items.prompt: Teachers use technology in class, and students take part more.
modelAnswers: The use of technology in class increases student participation.
Classroom technology use leads to greater student participation.
items.reason: “use” becomes “the use of” and “take part” becomes “participation”.

items.prompt: The implementation of the reduction of the consumption of plastic is a requirement for the achievement of the improvement of the environment.
options: Reducing plastic consumption is necessary to improve the environment.
We need to use less plastic to make the environment better.
The requirement of the implementation of plastic reduction is necessary for environmental improvement.
acceptedAnswers: Reducing plastic consumption is necessary to improve the environment.
items.reason: The best version keeps one clear noun phrase and uses the verb “improve”. The others are too informal or still too heavy.
items.hint: Look for the version that is formal but has fewer “of” phrases.
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. Which version is clearest?

items.prompt: The provision of an explanation of the cause of the failure of the system was given by the manager.
options: The manager explained why the system failed.
The manager provided an explanation of the cause of the system failure.
The manager gave the system an explanation of failure.
acceptedAnswers: The manager explained why the system failed.
items.reason: “The manager explained why the system failed” is short and clear, and keeps the meaning. Here, verbs work better than nouns.
items.hint: Who did what? Put that person first and use a verb.
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. Which version is clearest?

items.prompt: There was a decision by the committee for the postponement of the introduction of the new policy.
options: The committee decided to postpone the introduction of the new policy.
The committee's decision was a postponement of introduction of the policy.
The committee postponed and introduced the new policy.
acceptedAnswers: The committee decided to postpone the introduction of the new policy.
items.reason: The best version puts the committee first and uses the verbs “decided” and “postpone”. The last option changes the meaning.
items.hint: Start with “The committee” and use a verb.
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. Which version is clearest?

items.prompt: The utilisation of digital tools for the facilitation of the enhancement of student engagement is increasing.
options: Digital tools are increasingly used to improve student engagement.
Digital tool utilisation facilitation for engagement enhancement is increasing.
Students use digital tools more and more.
acceptedAnswers: Digital tools are increasingly used to improve student engagement.
items.reason: The best version keeps the meaning and is easy to read. The last option loses the idea of engagement.
items.hint: Which version keeps every idea but uses simple verbs?
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. Which version is clearest?

items.prompt: Consideration of the examination of the effects of the reduction of working hours on productivity is needed.
options: The effects of shorter working hours on productivity need to be examined.
Examination consideration of the reduction effects of hours is needed.
People should think about working less.
acceptedAnswers: The effects of shorter working hours on productivity need to be examined.
items.reason: The best version keeps one key noun phrase and uses the verb “examined”. The last option changes the meaning.
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. Which version is clearest?

items.prompt: The occurrence of an increase in the prevalence of obesity among children is a cause of concern for health authorities.
options: The rise in childhood obesity concerns health authorities.
An increase occurrence of prevalence of obesity in children happens.
Kids are getting fatter and doctors are worried.
acceptedAnswers: The rise in childhood obesity concerns health authorities.
items.reason: The best version is short, formal and keeps the meaning. The last option is too informal for an essay.
items.hint: Which version is both formal and short?
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. Which version is clearest?

items.prompt: The achievement of a reduction in the level of the consumption of energy by households is the aim of the programme.
modelAnswers: The programme aims to reduce household energy consumption.
The aim of the programme is to reduce how much energy households use.
items.reason: Turning “the achievement of a reduction” back into the verb “reduce” makes the sentence much easier to read.
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. How could you make it clearer?

items.prompt: The improvement of the quality of the communication between staff and management was the outcome of the introduction of weekly meetings.
modelAnswers: Introducing weekly meetings improved communication between staff and management.
Weekly meetings improved communication between staff and managers.
items.reason: Using the verb “improved” and putting the cause first makes the sentence clear.
items.hint: What caused what? Start with the cause.
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. How could you make it clearer?

items.prompt: The prevention of the spread of the infection requires the maintenance of hand hygiene by all visitors.
modelAnswers: All visitors need to maintain hand hygiene to prevent the spread of infection.
To stop the infection spreading, all visitors must keep their hands clean.
items.reason: Putting the people (visitors) first and using verbs makes the instruction clear.
items.question: This sentence is too heavy. How could you make it clearer?
